yoke.column.name: Yoke (roll / pitch)
yoke.column.note: yoke shaft between the handle centre and the right horn, entering the housing (roll/pitch)

unplaced.yoke.button.1: upper red push button on the left horn; number not documented
unplaced.yoke.button.2: lower red push button on the left horn; number not documented
unplaced.yoke.button.3: small oval button below the hat on the right horn; number not documented
unplaced.yoke.button.4: black rocker on the left horn (one direction, likely trim); direction/number not documented
unplaced.yoke.button.5: black rocker on the left horn (other direction, likely trim); direction/number not documented

source: JoyPro curated on the maker's photo (2026-10-11), the CLS-E NG yoke seen from the pilot's seat, front left, slightly from above: black handle in front, black motor housing behind; left horn with two red push buttons and a black rocker, right horn with a ribbed hat and a small oval button below it
mappingSource: catalog brunner.json (quick install guide https://shop.brunner-simulation.ch/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/BRUNNER_QuickInstallGuide_CLS-ENG-Yoke-1.pdf, product page https://brunner-innovation.swiss/product/cls-e-ng-yoke/): USB X = roll, Y = pitch; standalone default button 1 = trim reset, 4/5 = trim, 2/3 free. Which physical button is which number is not documented.
note: The button numbers per spot are guesses (trim 4/5 on the black rocker, 1-3 on the push buttons), so all five buttons are hidden candidates (map=low). The photo shows the same ribbed hat on the right horn as the CLS-E MK II yoke, but this catalog entry has no hat part (only 5 buttons); either the hat reports as some of the buttons or the catalog misses a hat part. Reported, not changed.
